q: Batch vs real-time vs streaming inference?
a: Batch: scheduled scoring of many rows (daily lists). Real-time: an API scores one request during a user action (loan application). Streaming: per-event scoring on a stream (card transactions). Choose the simplest the decision timing allows.

q: Shadow vs canary vs blue–green vs A/B?
a: Shadow: new model scores a copy of traffic, outputs only logged. Canary: gradually shift a small share of real traffic. Blue–green: switch all traffic between two environments at once, instant rollback. A/B: random split for weeks to measure business impact.

q: Where does latency usually come from in a real-time scoring API?
a: Feature lookups and external calls (credit bureau, other services), not the gradient-boosting model itself (~1 ms). Use an online feature store, timeouts and fallbacks, and log asynchronously.

q: Why export a model to ONNX?
a: Portable, version-stable format with fast inference (ONNX Runtime) callable from Java/C#/C++ services; must verify predictions match the original within tolerance.

q: What makes a batch scoring job production-grade?
a: Idempotent writes per date, model version and reasons stored with scores, validation before publishing (row counts, nulls, PSI vs last run), alerting, and keeping the previous scores if checks fail.
